4100.title: Daily Function Assessment (Frozen Shoulder)
4100.questionText: Automated evaluation of overall daily arm and shoulder function (QuickDASH).

options.label: Low limitation: minor disruption to daily tasks.
Moderate limitation: noticeable difficulty with daily chores or reaching.
High limitation: severe difficulty carrying out routine tasks or self-care.

4110.title: Symptom Duration & Past Self-Care
4110.questionText: How long have you been managing these shoulder stiffness symptoms?

options.label: Under 6 months of guided home stretching and light exercise.
6 months or more with persistent stiffness despite regular gentle exercise.

4200.title: Daily Function Assessment (Tendon / Impingement)

options.label: Low limitation: minor disruption to daily tasks.

4210.title: Response to Home Exercise
4210.questionText: How has your shoulder responded to rest and targeted exercise so far?

options.label: Less than 12 weeks of home exercises, or symptoms are gradually improving.
Severe pain or weakness continues despite 12 weeks of consistent home exercises.

4810.title: Home Exercise Plan: Frozen Shoulder
4810.primaryDiagnosis: Structured home exercise program for frozen shoulder: focus on daily gentle mobility and self-stretching (such as pendulum movements and passive wall climbs). Avoid aggressive or painful forcing into extreme ranges. Re-evaluate progress after 6 to 12 weeks.

4820.title: Home Exercise Plan: Tendon Strain / Impingement
4820.primaryDiagnosis: Structured home exercise program for shoulder tendon strain or pinching: progressive strengthening of rotator cuff muscles, shoulder blade stability exercises, and short-term activity adjustments to avoid repetitive overhead loading.

4830.title: Home Exercise Plan: General Recovery
4830.primaryDiagnosis: General shoulder recovery program: gradual mobility exercises, light strengthening, and posture awareness. If severe pain or functional limitations persist past 12 weeks of consistent exercise, seek an in-person physical examination.

4910.title: Evaluation Notice: Significant Tendon Tear
4910.primaryDiagnosis: Findings indicate a potential full-thickness rotator cuff tendon tear. While gentle home exercise helps maintain joint movement, significant tendon tears benefit from a professional medical scan (such as an MRI or ultrasound) to confirm tear size and guide recovery.

4920.title: Clinical Recommendation: Specialist Evaluation
4920.primaryDiagnosis: An in-person evaluation by a physical therapist or healthcare specialist is recommended based on the high level of difficulty reported with everyday arm activities.
